chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has livestock, does he sell their milk without measuring (by volume/weight)? He said, 'Yes, until it ceases or something of it is lost.'

key_terms.يَنْقَطِعَ: Ceases/ends (referring to the supply or quality)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell milk from livestock without measuring it exactly?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the sale of milk from livestock without fixed measurement (*kayl*), acknowledging the natural uncertainty (*gharar*) in yield. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between minor, inherent uncertainty in agricultural products and major uncertainty that invalidates contracts, permitting trade as long as the commodity is not entirely lost or spoiled.
